pr.title: Print only the version when field was not built from a checkout
pr.head: 5d0ff6a6cfb972cd6e4e56a1c531df27d4ee9289

summary: field --version tells you which build of the Field CLI is running. Its first line is the version from package.json, followed in parentheses by the Git commit the build came from, so that during development you can see whether the code you are running is the code in your checkout.

A release install is the other way to get Field: install.sh downloads GitHub's source archive of a version's tag, unpacks it into a directory of its own, and builds it there. That archive has no .git, so the build has no commit to name, and the first line read field 0.3.0  (not a git checkout). Release installs are now the usual install, so the parenthetical described the normal case as if something were missing.

This pull request prints the version alone when the build has no commit, and leaves a build from a checkout exactly as it was. The build script's log line drops the same phrase, and docs/cli.md shows the release line in its example. How a build decides whether it has a commit does not change.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Build stamp: dist/build-info.json, which scripts/stamp-build.mjs writes at the end of pnpm build. It holds the commit, branch, and count of uncommitted files the build saw, or {} when Git finds no commit.
  • Checkout: a Git clone of the repository, built in place.
  • Release install: a version's source archive, unpacked and built by install.sh, with no .git.
  • Drift: the checkout moving after the build, by a new commit or by edits, which field --version reports beside the stamped commit.

groups.title: The first line of field --version
groups.kicker: The formatter prints the version alone when the build has no commit
intro: formatVersionReport turns the version report into the text field --version prints. Its first line is field <version>, plus a parenthetical describing the build's commit when there is one: the short commit, the branch unless HEAD is detached, the count of uncommitted files at build time, and any drift since.

When the report carries no commit, the parenthetical used to say not a git checkout. It is now left out, and the line is the version alone. The report's fields, and the code that fills them, are unchanged, so nothing about which builds have a commit moves.

files.note: The formatter's build string becomes undefined when there is no commit, and the first line drops its parenthetical in that case.

checks.text: A report has no commit in two ways. Run from dist/, buildIdentity reads the build stamp and, when the stamp has no commit, falls back to asking Git at the package root, which finds none in an archive either. Run from source, it asks Git directly. Drift fields are set only beside a stamped commit, so leaving out the parenthetical drops no drift report.

The review built a git archive of this head outside any repository, installed it with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, and ran node dist/cli.js --version: the first line was field 0.3.0. In a detached checkout of the head, a clean build printed field 0.3.0  (5d0ff6a), and the dirty and drifted cases printed the forms in the overview's table.

files.note: Two formatter cases: a report with no commit prints field 0.3.0, and one with a commit and branch prints field 0.3.0  (aaaa111 on main).

checks.text: These test the formatter alone. No automated test runs field --version from a build without .git; the release-install tests in src/install.test.ts run the real stamp script in such a tree but discard its output.

groups.title: The build stamp's log line
groups.kicker: pnpm build stops printing "not a git checkout" for a release
intro: scripts/stamp-build.mjs runs at the end of pnpm build. It asks Git for the commit at the package root, writes the build stamp, and logs one line. A release install builds twice, once from the prepare step of pnpm install and once from pnpm run build, so the old phrase appeared twice during every release install.

Only the log line changes. The stamp's JSON is the same {} for a build with no commit, so the two readers of it, field --version and the report_build check in install.sh that prints cli-current or cli-stale, read it as before.

files.note: The log line adds the short commit in parentheses only when the stamp has one.

checks.text: The archive build logged stamped dist/build-info.json with nothing after it and wrote {}; a checkout build logged stamped dist/build-info.json (5d0ff6a). A search of the repository found nothing that parses this line.

The detection above this line is unchanged, and it has a gap the review lists as a suggestion: git -C <root> rev-parse HEAD searches upward, so a release unpacked inside another Git work tree, such as a home directory kept in Git, stamps that repository's commit. An archive of this head built that way printed field 0.3.0  (948b7e3 on main, 1 file uncommitted), as the base does. Asking Git only when the package root holds a .git entry, the test install.sh uses, would close it.

groups.title: The documented example
groups.kicker: docs/cli.md shows the release line and describes what a checkout adds
intro: The command reference's example of field --version now shows a release install's output, and the paragraph after it gives the checkout form as an inline example.

files.note: The example's first line becomes field 0.3.0, and the text says a build from a checkout adds its commit.

checks.text: The example matches the archive build's output line for line. Its remote line is the form the formatter prints for the default remote with no login, and the inline checkout example uses the formatter's two spaces before the parenthesis.
